v.rationale: All three implementations share nearly the same architecture: an invokable controller, a FormRequest with filters(), an invokable BuildSalesReport, #[Scope] attribute scopes, an OrderStatus enum with Rule::enum, the #[Fillable] attribute and Number::currency. Each test suite passes, and all three produce identical figures on my probe dataset, which includes an order with no items, multi-line orders, country filtering and inclusive day boundaries. The ranking therefore rests on edge-case behaviour and code quality. impl-1 is first: its 'nullable' rules accept empty query strings and fall back to defaults instead of returning 422, it uses strict Y-m-d dates, and it builds the report with direct joins from orders using join-safe qualified scope columns. Its weaknesses are that top customers have no id, it uses an untyped array parameter, and it does not echo the filters back. impl-3 is second: it has the best tests and the most readable service, but empty parameters return 422, it rewrites the scope chain at BuildSalesReport.php:29 instead of reusing the $orders closure, the item factory runs an extra query, and it has small ceremony and import-style issues. impl-2 is third: it shares the empty-parameter 422 problem, and its lenient 'date' rule accepts relative or ambiguous dates such as 'tomorrow'. It also has an inconsistent money shape in revenue_per_country, where cents/formatted are spread into the row instead of nested as in the other lists, and it duplicates the scope chain. On the plus side it does not expose customer emails and it trims the country input.
